cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) names the feast and his own betrayal in one breath, and the feast is the one Yahuah (the LORD) gave to Moses and Aaron in Egypt. Matthew sets his death inside the passover Moses received, and nothing in either verse sets that feast aside.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) gives Moses and Aaron the passover in Egypt, the feast Yahusha (Jesus) says is two days away.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) does not set the feast aside: he has his disciples prepare it and says *I will keep the passover at thy house with my disciples* (Matthew 26:18). The keeping goes back to where Yahuah (the LORD) first spoke it to Moses and Aaron in Egypt, and he keeps it as it was given.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) speaks the passover to Moses and Aaron in Egypt, the feast the disciples ask where to prepare.

cards.prose: Two days before the feast he says he will be betrayed to be crucified. John the Baptist had already pointed at him and said *Behold the Lamb of Elohim (God)*, and the feast he names is the one in which a lamb is killed.
cards.member_sentence: John the Baptist calls Yahusha (Jesus) the Lamb of Elohim (God), the lamb of the passover he is now two days from.

cards.prose: The disciples ask where to prepare the passover, which means a lamb. John the Baptist had pointed at Yahusha (Jesus) as he walked and said *Behold the Lamb of Elohim (God)!*, so the lamb of the feast and the one who sits down to eat it are named together.
cards.member_sentence: John the Baptist points at Yahusha (Jesus) as he walks and calls him the Lamb of Elohim (God).

cards.prose: Two days before, he said the feast was near and he would be betrayed to be crucified. In John the feast has come: *the preparation of the passover*, and he is brought out and shown to the Yahudim (Jews) with the words *Behold your King!*
cards.member_sentence: John dates the day of the judgment seat as the preparation of the passover, the feast Yahusha (Jesus) named in Matthew.
cards.flag: Old note pointed at the unbroken bone (John 19:36); the target on the card is 19:14, so the card is written to the preparation of the passover that verse names.

cards.prose: The preparation Matthew begins here ends at the cross in John, where the things done are said to be done *that the scripture should be fulfilled*, and the words are *A bone of him shall not be broken*. It is the care the passover lamb was given in Egypt, now laid on the one the disciples are preparing the meal for.
cards.member_sentence: John says not a bone of him is broken, the rule that was laid on the passover lamb in Egypt.

cards.prose: Paul speaks of the feast as a feast that stands: the old leaven is purged and the unleavened lump is kept. In the middle of it he says *Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us*, which is the lamb of the feast Yahusha (Jesus) names two days ahead.
cards.member_sentence: Paul names Messiah (Christ) as the passover lamb sacrificed, while still speaking of old leaven purged and unleavened bread kept.

cards.prose: The disciples ask where to prepare the passover, and Paul writes that *Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us*, naming the lamb. He goes on in the next verse, *Therefore let us keep the feast* (1 Corinthians 5:8), so the feast stays and its lamb has been named.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed and in the next verse tells them to keep the feast.

cards.prose: Peter says what the price was not, *silver and gold*, and a verse on says what it was, the blood of Messiah (Christ), *as of a lamb without blemish and without spot* (1 Peter 1:19). That is the kind of lamb the passover called for, and Matthew's two days are the count down to it.
cards.member_sentence: Peter says redemption was not paid in silver and gold but in the blood of Messiah (Christ), as of a lamb without blemish.

cards.prose: They are preparing the passover meal, and Peter says redemption did not come by *silver and gold* but by the blood of Messiah (Christ), *as of a lamb without blemish and without spot* (1 Peter 1:19). A lamb without blemish is how the passover lamb was chosen.
cards.member_sentence: Peter says they were redeemed not with silver and gold but with the blood of Messiah (Christ), a lamb without blemish.

cards.prose: In the same breath as the feast he says he is to be betrayed and crucified, and Revelation shows the lamb standing in the midst of the throne *as it had been slain*. The one given up at the passover is the one John sees still carrying the mark of it.
cards.member_phrase: stood a Lamb as it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes
cards.member_sentence: John sees a Lamb standing in the midst of the throne as it had been slain, the one Matthew's verse sends to the passover.

cards.prose: The disciples ask where to eat the passover, and in Revelation the voices cry *Worthy is the Lamb that was slain*. The lamb of the table in Matthew and the Lamb in John's vision are the same lamb, now given power, riches, wisdom, strength, honour, glory and blessing.
cards.member_sentence: Revelation's voices call the Lamb that was slain worthy of power, riches, wisdom, strength, honour, glory and blessing.

cards.prose: Matthew gives the day he is betrayed to be crucified, and Revelation shows who stands before the throne because of it. They came out of great tribulation and have *made them white in the blood of the Lamb*, so the blood begun at the feast is still washing.
cards.member_phrase: have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb
cards.member_sentence: A great multitude out of great tribulation has washed its robes white in the blood of the Lamb whose death Matthew's verse foretells.

cards.prose: Matthew shows the disciples preparing the passover for the one whose blood is to be shed, and Revelation shows what that blood does. Those who came out of great tribulation have washed their robes and *made them white in the blood of the Lamb*.
cards.member_phrase: have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb
cards.member_sentence: Those who came out of great tribulation wash their robes white in the blood of the Lamb, the lamb of the feast now being prepared.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says he is to be betrayed and crucified at the feast, and Revelation says what the lamb's blood did. The accuser of the brethren was overcome *by the blood of the Lamb*, and by *the word of their testimony*, and those who overcame him *loved not their lives unto the death*.
cards.member_sentence: Those who overcame the accuser did it by the blood of the Lamb and loved not their lives unto death.

cards.prose: The disciples prepare the passover and Revelation says what the Lamb's blood has done: the accuser was overcome *by the blood of the Lamb* and *the word of their testimony*. The ones who overcame *loved not their lives unto the death*, as the Lamb gave his.
cards.member_sentence: The accuser is overcome by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony, by those who loved not their lives.

cards.prose: Two days before the feast he says he will be betrayed to be crucified, and Isaiah had already described the man who goes to it without a word. *Brought as a lamb to the slaughter*, he opens not his mouth, and the feast he names is the one that kills a lamb.
cards.member_phrase: yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's afflicted servant is brought like a lamb to the slaughter and does not open his mouth, the way Yahusha (Jesus) goes to the feast.

cards.prose: The disciples ask where to prepare the passover, and Isaiah had described the lamb long before: *he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter*, and as a sheep before her shearers he opens not his mouth. The one eating the meal is the one brought to it silent.
cards.member_phrase: yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's afflicted servant is brought as a lamb to the slaughter and is silent, as the sheep before her shearers.

cards.prose: Abraham, going up the mountain with his son, said *Elohim (God) will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering*. Read beside Matthew, the lamb that Elohim (God) provides for himself is standing at the table two days before the passover, saying he will be betrayed to be crucified.
cards.member_sentence: Abraham tells his son that Elohim (God) will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering, long before the passover lamb of Egypt.

cards.prose: On the first day of unleavened bread the disciples ask where the lamb is to be prepared. Abraham's answer to his son long before was *Elohim (God) will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering*, and the lamb at this table is the one Elohim (God) provided.
cards.member_sentence: Abraham says Elohim (God) will provide himself a lamb, the answer the passover meal in Matthew begins to give.

cards.prose: Revelation closes the lamb's story at a wedding, *the marriage of the Lamb is come*, and his wife has made herself ready. Matthew begins it at the passover with Yahusha (Jesus) saying he will be betrayed to be crucified, so the same lamb runs from one verse to the other.
cards.member_sentence: Revelation ends the lamb's story with the marriage of the Lamb, the same lamb Matthew's verse sends to the passover.

cards.prose: The disciples prepare the passover meal and Revelation ends at a wedding feast, *the marriage of the Lamb is come*, and his wife has made herself ready. The lamb who sits at this table is the one the feast in Revelation is named for.
cards.member_sentence: Revelation's marriage of the Lamb comes at the end of the story whose passover meal Matthew's disciples are preparing.

cards.prose: These are the sayings Yahusha (Jesus) has just finished, and this parable is among them: a householder lets his vineyard out to husbandmen, and when his servants come for the fruit they are beaten and killed. The plot that opens in the verses after this one is that parable being acted out.
cards.member_phrase: There was a certain householder, which planted a vineyard, and hedged it round about
cards.member_sentence: The householder's vineyard let out to husbandmen who beat and kill his servants is the story the council of Matthew 26 is about to live out.

cards.prose: He had told the leaders to their faces what was coming: *some of them ye shall kill and crucify*. In the next verses the chief priests and elders gather at the high priest's palace to consult how to kill him, so the plot follows the warning and does not surprise him.
cards.member_phrase: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) warns the scribes and leaders that some of those he sends they will kill and crucify, the plot he then names in Matthew 26.

cards.prose: The psalm asks the question the next verses answer. In Matthew the chief priests, scribes and elders gather and consult against Yahusha (Jesus), and the psalm had already pictured the rulers who *take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed* (Psalm 2:2).
cards.member_sentence: The psalm asks why the heathen rage and the people imagine a vain thing, and goes on to rulers taking counsel against the anointed.
cards.flag: Target is Psalm 2:1 only; the old note's point (the kings taking counsel against Yahuah and his anointed) is in 2:2, which the prose quotes with its citation.

cards.prose: This is the council behind Matthew's council. John shows the chief priests and Pharisees first gathering because *this man doeth many miracles*, and Caiaphas, the high priest that year, is already saying that it is expedient for one man to die for the people.
cards.member_sentence: John shows the chief priests and Pharisees gathering a council over his miracles, the first meeting that leads to the one at Caiaphas's palace.

cards.prose: Right after the sayings are finished, the first thing he speaks of is the passover, and the passover begins where this verse begins, with Yahuah (the LORD) speaking to Moses and Aaron in Egypt. The feast he names two days ahead is the one Moses was given.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) speaks to Moses and Aaron in Egypt, the opening of the passover Yahusha (Jesus) names in the next verse.

cards.prose: John dates this supper for us, *six days before the passover*, and puts it at Bethany with Lazarus at the table. In John the woman is Mary and the ointment goes on his feet, and Judas Iscariot is the one who complains; Matthew has it poured on his head with the disciples complaining.
cards.member_sentence: John dates the Bethany supper six days before the passover, names Mary as the woman and Judas Iscariot as the one who objects.

cards.prose: Luke has a woman with an alabaster box at a meal too, but it is in a Pharisee's house, she is weeping at his feet, and the objection is about who she is. Matthew's meal is in the house of Simon the leper and the objection is about waste, so these read as two different suppers.
cards.member_sentence: Luke's woman with an alabaster box comes to a Pharisee's table and weeps at his feet, a separate meal from the one in Bethany.

cards.prose: When Samuel took his vial of oil and poured it on a head, it set a man apart as captain over Yahuah's (the LORD's) inheritance. A woman pours oil on Yahusha's (Jesus's) head at Bethany, and the old anointing of a king sits beside her. He says what he saw in it: *she did it for my burial* (Matthew 26:12).
cards.member_phrase: hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance
cards.member_sentence: Samuel pours oil on a head to anoint a captain over Yahuah's (the LORD's) inheritance, the act the woman at Bethany repeats.

cards.prose: Samuel's horn of oil on David's head, in the midst of his brethren, was the anointing of the one Yahuah (the LORD) had chosen, and the Spirit came upon David from that day. Oil on Yahusha's (Jesus's) head at Bethany reads line on line with it, and he names a second meaning, his burial.
cards.member_phrase: anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of Yahuah (LORD) came upon David from that day forward
cards.member_sentence: Samuel anoints David with the horn of oil in the midst of his brethren, and the Spirit of Yahuah (the LORD) comes upon him.

cards.prose: The psalm speaks to a king whose throne is *for ever and ever* (Psalm 45:6) and who is anointed *with the oil of gladness above thy fellows*. The woman pours precious ointment on Yahusha's (Jesus's) head while the disciples count the cost, and the psalm's anointing stands behind what she did.
cards.member_sentence: The psalm names the king anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows, the anointing beside the ointment poured at Bethany.

cards.prose: The disciples say the ointment should have been given to the poor, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers with Moses' own words, *ye have the poor always with you* (Matthew 26:11). The commandment in that verse to open the hand wide to the poor is not set aside; he is naming one hour that will not come again.
cards.member_phrase: the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor
cards.member_sentence: Moses says the poor will never cease out of the land and commands the open hand toward them, the words Yahusha (Jesus) draws on.

cards.prose: Matthew gives Judas's walk to the chief priests. John says what had been put into his heart first, *the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot*, the thought to betray. He still went and asked *What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you* (Matthew 26:15), so the choice and the price were his.
cards.member_sentence: John says the devil had put the betrayal into the heart of Judas Iscariot before the supper ended.

cards.prose: John shows the table behind Matthew's bargain. Yahusha (Jesus) gives Judas the sop, *Satan entered into him*, and Judas is told *That thou doest, do quickly*. The thirty pieces were already agreed, and now Judas goes out, and it was night.
cards.member_sentence: After the sop Satan enters Judas, and Yahusha (Jesus) tells him to do quickly what he does, the table moment behind the thirty pieces.

cards.prose: Mark tells the same question the same way and adds what kind of day it was, *when they killed the passover*. The disciples ask about preparing the meal on the day the lambs were slain, so the supper and the lamb come together in one day.
cards.member_phrase: when they killed the passover, his disciples said unto him, Where wilt thou that we go and prepare
cards.member_sentence: Mark adds that the first day of unleavened bread was when they killed the passover, the day the disciples ask where to prepare it.

cards.prose: Luke gives the same day and says it as a requirement, *the passover must be killed*. The disciples ask where to prepare it because the day itself asked for it, and Yahusha (Jesus) keeps the feast as the day required.
cards.member_sentence: Luke says the day of unleavened bread came when the passover must be killed, the same day the disciples ask in Matthew.

cards.prose: Matthew has the disciples preparing the passover, and Paul says what happened at that meal, that *the same night in which he was betrayed* Yahusha (Jesus) took bread. Paul says he received it from Yahusha (Jesus) and handed it on as it was given.
cards.member_phrase: the same night in which he was betrayed took bread
cards.member_sentence: Paul says he received from Yahusha (Jesus) what he delivered, that on the night he was betrayed he took bread.
cards.flag: Source is 26:17 but the pairing is the supper's account; placed in the last-supper thread with the other cup and bread cards rather than the lamb group.

cards.prose: At the table he will say *this is my blood of the new testament* (Matthew 26:28), and Moses had used almost the same words when he sprinkled the people, *Behold the blood of the covenant*. That covenant was made *concerning all these words*, the commandments, so the words at the table are Moses' own.
cards.member_phrase: Behold the blood of the covenant, which Yahuah (LORD) hath made with you concerning all these words
cards.member_sentence: Moses sprinkles the blood on the people and says it is the blood of the covenant Yahuah (the LORD) made concerning all these words.

cards.prose: The new covenant has an address on it already: *with the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* and *the house of Yahudah (Judah)*, both houses. Two verses on Yahuah (the LORD) says how it is kept, *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts* (Jeremiah 31:33), the commandments written inside.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah).

cards.prose: The cup is *shed for many* (Matthew 26:28), and Isaiah says who the many are. The servant's soul is made an offering for sin, *he shall see his seed*, and *he shall bear their iniquities* (Isaiah 53:11). The many are the seed he sees.
cards.member_phrase: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says the servant makes his soul an offering for sin and shall see his seed, the many of the cup.

cards.prose: Mark tells the arrest in nearly the same words and adds the scribes to those who sent the crowd. In both, Judas comes while Yahusha (Jesus) is still speaking, and the swords and staves are sent by the chief priests and elders, not raised by the people.
cards.member_phrase: cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders
cards.member_sentence: Mark has Judas arrive with a great multitude with swords and staves sent from the chief priests, the scribes and the elders.

cards.prose: Luke has Judas walking *before them* to kiss him, and gives two things Matthew leaves out. Yahusha (Jesus) says *Judas, betrayest thou the Son of Adam with a kiss?* (Luke 22:48), and when the ear is cut off he touches it and heals him (Luke 22:51).
cards.member_phrase: he that was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them, and drew near unto Yahusha (Jesus) to kiss him
cards.member_sentence: Luke has Judas go before the multitude to kiss him, and adds the question put to Judas and the healing of the ear.

cards.prose: John says why Judas could lead them, he *knew the place*, because Yahusha (Jesus) went there often with his disciples. John also shows him not caught off guard, but *knowing all things that should come upon him* (John 18:4), he goes out and asks *Whom seek ye?* (John 18:4)
cards.member_sentence: John says Judas knew the garden because Yahusha (Jesus) often went there with his disciples.

cards.prose: Judas arrives at the head of the crowd, and the sign he gave them was a kiss (Matthew 26:48). Proverbs already knew the two kinds of touch, *the wounds of a friend* and *the kisses of an enemy*, and this kiss, from one who ate at the table, belongs to the second kind.
cards.member_sentence: Proverbs says a friend's wounds are faithful and an enemy's kisses are deceitful, the kind of kiss Judas gives.

cards.prose: David's psalm describes a betrayal that hurt because it was no stranger's: *it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance* (Psalm 55:13). Judas comes to Yahusha (Jesus) with the crowd, one of the twelve, and is still called *Friend* (Matthew 26:50).
cards.member_phrase: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it
cards.member_sentence: The psalmist says it was no enemy but his own equal and acquaintance who reproached him, the grief of Judas's coming.

cards.prose: Genesis 9:6 gives the measure of the sword, blood shed by man is answered by man. When a disciple draws his sword in the garden Yahusha (Jesus) says *all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword* (Matthew 26:52), and tells him to put it up. He refuses the sword to save himself.
cards.member_sentence: Genesis gives the measure that whoever sheds man's blood has his own shed, the rule behind the word about the sword.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) had told them at the mount of Olives that it is written *I will smite the shepherd* (Matthew 26:31), and now the crowd with swords and staves has come. Zechariah puts the sword's awaking in the mouth of Yahuah (the LORD), and in Matthew *all the disciples forsook him, and fled* (Matthew 26:56), the sheep scattered.
cards.member_phrase: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) bids the sword smite the shepherd and scatter the sheep, the verse Matthew quotes at 26:31.

cards.prose: He could ask the Father for *more than twelve legions of angels* (Matthew 26:53), and he does not. John gives the reason in his own words, he lays down his life, and a verse on, *No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself* (John 10:18), a charge he received from his Father.
cards.member_sentence: John says the Father loves him because he lays down his life, which no man takes from him.
cards.flag: John 10:17 is also a member of the Gethsemane thread from 26:36; here it is placed with the arrest because the card's source is 26:47 and the point is 26:53.

cards.prose: Mark tells it the same way and adds the full list around the high priest, *all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes* were assembled. The men who sit to judge him are the whole court, and Mark says in the next verses they sought witness and found none.
cards.member_phrase: and with him were assembled all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes
cards.member_sentence: Mark adds that all the chief priests, the elders and the scribes were assembled with the high priest.

cards.prose: Luke has the same walk to the high priest's house and puts Peter in the same sentence, *Peter followed afar off*, as Matthew does in the next verse. While the court sits, a disciple is out in the courtyard watching, and his own trial is about to begin.
cards.member_sentence: Luke brings Yahusha (Jesus) into the high priest's house with Peter following afar off.

cards.prose: Luke has the men who held him mocking and striking him, and sets it before the elders and chief priests gather at day. Matthew sets the spitting after the verdict. They agree that he was struck and made the target of a joke by the men who held him.
cards.member_sentence: Luke says the men holding Yahusha (Jesus) mocked and struck him, in his own order of events.
cards.flag: Luke and Matthew order the mocking differently (Luke before the morning council, Matthew after the verdict); the prose says so without choosing between them.

cards.prose: Matthew goes straight to Caiaphas, and John says they led him *to Annas first*, the father in law of Caiaphas. John adds that Caiaphas was the one who counseled *it was expedient that one man should die for the people* (John 18:14), so what the court would decide had been said before he stood in it.
cards.member_sentence: John says they led him to Annas first, father in law to Caiaphas, the high priest that year.

cards.prose: John gives the question the high priest put to him, *of his disciples, and of his doctrine*, and the answer, *I spake openly to the world* (John 18:20). He then sends the high priest to those who heard him, *ask them which heard me* (John 18:21), which is where witnesses belong.
cards.member_sentence: John records the high priest asking Yahusha (Jesus) about his disciples and his doctrine.

cards.prose: He is led to Caiaphas, and the answer he will give there is David's verse, *sitting on the right hand of power* (Matthew 26:64). David calls him *my Lord*, and Yahuah (the LORD) tells him to sit at his right hand, so two are in the verse, the one who speaks and the one who sits. The man led away bound is claiming that seat.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) tells the one David addresses to sit at his right hand, the seat Yahusha (Jesus) claims before the council.

cards.prose: Led before Caiaphas, he answers with Daniel's vision of one *like the Son of Adam* who came *with the clouds of heaven*. Daniel keeps the word *like*, and in the next verse says what is given him, *dominion, and glory, and a kingdom* (Daniel 7:14), and that is all Daniel's own page gives.
cards.member_phrase: one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days
cards.member_sentence: Daniel sees one like the Son of Adam come with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of days, the verse Yahusha (Jesus) draws on.

cards.prose: Matthew says *Yahusha (Jesus) held his peace* (Matthew 26:63), and Isaiah had already written the man who is afflicted and yet opens not his mouth. Brought as a lamb to the slaughter, he is silent before the high priest because that is the servant's way.
cards.member_phrase: yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's afflicted servant opens not his mouth, the silence Yahusha (Jesus) keeps before the high priest.

cards.prose: Matthew says *Then did they spit in his face, and buffeted him* (Matthew 26:67). Isaiah's speaker had said he hid not his face *from shame and spitting*, giving his back to the smiters. He gave himself to it, and nobody took the choice from him.
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's servant gives his back to the smiters and hides not his face from shame and spitting.

cards.prose: Moses' rule is that a matter is established *at the mouth of two witnesses*. Matthew's council could not meet it, *though many false witnesses came, yet found they none* (Matthew 26:60), and the high priest asks *what further need have we of witnesses?* (Matthew 26:65). The Torah stood and their court did not keep it.
cards.member_phrase: at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established
cards.member_sentence: The Torah requires two or three witnesses before a matter is established, a rule the council could not meet.

cards.prose: Mark names the woman as one of *the maids of the high priest* and has Peter *beneath in the palace*, in the courtyard below the room where Yahusha (Jesus) is being tried. Peter's first question comes from a servant of the house whose master is judging his teacher.
cards.member_sentence: Mark places Peter beneath in the palace, where one of the high priest's maids comes to him.

cards.prose: Luke has Peter following *afar off* and adds what Matthew leaves out. After the denial Yahusha (Jesus) *turned, and looked upon Peter* (Luke 22:61), and Peter *went out, and wept bitterly* (Luke 22:62). The look is the way back.
cards.member_sentence: Luke puts Peter in the high priest's house, following afar off, before the look Yahusha (Jesus) gives him.
cards.flag: Target Luke 22:54 only carries Peter following afar off; the look the old note meant is Luke 22:61-62, quoted with citation.

cards.prose: John says Peter did not go in alone. Another disciple, *known unto the high priest*, went in with Yahusha (Jesus) and then *spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter* (John 18:16), so the door that opened to the question at the fire was opened for him by a friend.
cards.member_phrase: that disciple was known unto the high priest, and went in with Yahusha (Jesus) into the palace of the high priest
cards.member_sentence: John says another disciple known to the high priest went in with Yahusha (Jesus) and later brought Peter in.

cards.prose: John puts Peter at the fire of coals among the servants and officers, and the question there is the one Matthew has, *Art not thou also one of his disciples?* The answer in John is a flat *I am not*.
cards.member_phrase: Art not thou also one of his disciples? He denied it, and said, I am not
cards.member_sentence: John has Peter warming himself at the fire, asked if he is a disciple, and denying it.

cards.prose: Peter spoke at the supper with his whole heart, *yet will I never be offended*, and a few hours later he said *I do not know the man* (Matthew 26:72). Yahusha (Jesus) had told him exactly what was coming, *before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice* (Matthew 26:34), so the fall was no surprise to him.
cards.member_sentence: Peter's promise that he would never be offended is the saying his three denials answer in the same chapter.
cards.flag: Target is Matthew 26:33 in this same chapter, the prediction the denial answers; written as the two verses standing together.

cards.prose: Peter denied three times and is asked three times, *lovest thou me?*, after the resurrection. Each answer gets a charge, *Feed my lambs*, and *Feed my sheep* (John 21:16). The sheep that stumbled is not cast off, he is given the sheep to tend.
cards.member_phrase: lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Adonai (Lord); thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) asks Peter if he loves him and gives him lambs to feed, the restoration after the denial.

cards.prose: Peter went out and wept bitterly, and the psalm speaks to that. David wrote that *a broken and a contrite heart* is what Elohim (God) will not despise, and Peter, the sheep that stumbled, is met by that and not by condemnation.
cards.member_sentence: David says the sacrifice Elohim (God) wants is a broken spirit and a contrite heart he will not despise.

cards.prose: Joel's call is *turn ye even to me with all your heart*, and a verse on, *rend your heart, and not your garments* (Joel 2:13). The high priest rent his clothes earlier in the chapter; the one who answers Joel's call is Peter, who went out and wept.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) calls through Joel for a turn with all the heart, with weeping, the turning Peter makes.

new_threads.title: The plot against Yahusha (Jesus) and the passover lamb
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. Two days before the feast, Yahusha (Jesus) says to his disciples:

*Ye know that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of Adam is betrayed to be crucified.* (Matthew 26:2)

The feast he names is the one Yahuah (the LORD) gave to Moses and Aaron in Egypt, and it begins with a lamb taken for each house:

*Speak ye unto all the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for an house:* (Exodus 12:3)

Abraham had already said on the mountain what Elohim (God) would do about the lamb:

*My son, Elohim (God) will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering* (Genesis 22:8)

John the Baptist points at the man walking by and calls him that lamb, and Isaiah had written how the lamb would go:

*Behold the Lamb of Elohim (God), which taketh away the sin of the world* (John 1:29)

*he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth* (Isaiah 53:7)

Paul speaks of the feast as still the feast, the old leaven purged and the lump unleavened, and names the lamb in the middle of it:

*For even Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us* (1 Corinthians 5:7)

The feast is not undone by his death, it is filled. Around it the rulers gather and plot. They are the chief priests, the scribes and the elders at the palace of Caiaphas, and the people they fear are not the ones in the plot:

*And consulted that they might take Yahusha (Jesus) by subtilty, and kill him.* (Matthew 26:4)

The psalm had pictured the same gathering:

*the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed* (Psalm 2:2)

And he had told them to their faces where it was heading:

*and some of them ye shall kill and crucify* (Matthew 23:34)

John shows the council before this one, gathered over the miracles, with Caiaphas saying one man should die for the people. The plot belongs to the system that held the court, and the lamb goes to it the way the older words said.

new_threads.title: The anointing at Bethany
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. In the house of Simon the leper a woman pours ointment on Yahusha's (Jesus's) head, and the disciples call it waste:

*There came unto him a woman having an alabaster box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head, as he sat at meat.* (Matthew 26:7)

Oil on a head is the oldest way the text sets a man apart. Samuel did it for a captain over Yahuah's (the LORD's) inheritance:

*Then Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured it upon his head* (1 Samuel 10:1)

and for David, in the middle of his brothers:

*Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of Yahuah (LORD) came upon David from that day forward* (1 Samuel 16:13)

The psalm speaks to a king in the same words of oil:

*therefore Elohim (God), thy Elohim (God), hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows* (Psalm 45:7)

So the oil at Bethany sits beside the anointing of kings, and Yahusha (Jesus) says what he saw in it as well:

*For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial.* (Matthew 26:12)

When the disciples say the money should have gone to the poor, he answers from Moses, and the commandment in that same verse is not set aside:

*For the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land* (Deuteronomy 15:11)

*For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.* (Matthew 26:11)

John dates the same supper six days before the passover and names the woman Mary. Luke's woman with an alabaster box comes to a Pharisee's table and is a different meal.

new_threads.title: The arrest in the garden
new_threads.summary_md:
In the garden Yahusha (Jesus) is still speaking when the crowd arrives:

*And while he yet spake, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and elders of the people.* (Matthew 26:47)

John says why Judas could lead them there, and that Yahusha (Jesus) was not caught off guard:

*And Judas also, which betrayed him, knew the place: for Yahusha (Jesus) ofttimes resorted thither with his disciples.* (John 18:2)

A disciple draws a sword and strikes the servant of the high priest. Luke adds that Yahusha (Jesus) touched the ear and healed him:

*And Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, Suffer ye thus far. And he touched his ear, and healed him.* (Luke 22:51)

Then he says to the one who struck:

*Then said Yahusha (Jesus) unto him, Put up again thy sword into his place: for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.* (Matthew 26:52)

It ain't new. Noah was given the measure of the sword long before:

*Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of Elohim (God) made he man.* (Genesis 9:6)

He refuses the sword, and not because he cannot call for help:

*Thinkest thou that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels?* (Matthew 26:53)

John gives the reason in his own words, a life laid down by the one who has it:

*No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father.* (John 10:18)

The swords and staves come from the chief priests and elders, and Mark adds the scribes, the rulers who held the court. Judas chose his part, and the crowd of the people is not the plot. The one they come to take is not taken, he gives himself, as a charge he received from his Father.

new_threads.title: Peter's denial and his restoration
new_threads.summary_md:
At the supper Peter says what he means with all his heart:

*Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended.* (Matthew 26:33)

Yahusha (Jesus) tells him what the night will do:

*Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.* (Matthew 26:34)

It comes as he said. In the palace Peter is asked and denies with an oath:

*And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.* (Matthew 26:72)

Matthew ends the scene with the cock crowing and the man outside:

*And Peter remembered the word of Yahusha (Jesus), which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.* (Matthew 26:75)

Luke says what happened in between, a look:

*And Yahusha (Lord) turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of Yahusha (Lord), how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.* (Luke 22:61)

David had written what meets a heart broken like that:

*The sacrifices of Elohim (God) are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise.* (Psalm 51:17)

Joel had called for the same turn, in the heart and not in the clothes:

*And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)* (Joel 2:13)

After the resurrection Peter is asked three times, once for each denial, and each time he is given a charge:

*Simon, son of Jonah, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Adonai (Lord); thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs* (John 21:15)

Peter fell and wept and was restored. He is a sheep that stumbled, and he is not condemned. The other gospels add their own detail, and they agree on the fire, the three questions and the three answers.
